description: P7 source table for the 1900 labour market: census occupation groups (Webb 1911), 1900 earnings for the new professions (Historical Statistics of the United States), and the minimum-wage coverage example (FLSA 1938). Every row carries its source, locator and status (sourced, or provisional with the reasoning in its note). Flax, hemp and jute are not sourced here (fibre good deferred by the designer, plan Q15-Q16).

sources.title: The New Dictionary of Statistics: a complement to the fourth edition of Mulhall's Dictionary of Statistics
sources.author: Augustus Duncan Webb
sources.publisher: London: G. Routledge; New York: E. P. Dutton, 1911
sources.license: Public domain (published 1911; Internet Archive copyright status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT)
sources.attribution: Webb (1911), article "Occupations", pp. 428-448; Webb's own sources are his bracketed numbers, given in each locator.
sources.notes: Read from the page images of the Internet Archive scan (PDF page = book page + 16). Webb warns that classifications differ between countries.

sources.title: Historical Statistics of the United States, Colonial Times to 1970, Bicentennial Edition, Part 1, Chapter D: Labor
sources.author: U.S. Bureau of the Census
sources.license: Public domain (work of the United States Government)
sources.attribution: U.S. Bureau of the Census (1975), series D 739-764 (Lebergott) and D 779-793 (Douglas, Real Wages in the United States, 1930).
sources.notes: PDF page = book page - 120. Lebergott's 1900-1928 estimates are not comparable with the later BLS figures (the table's footnote); only 1900-1901 values are used.

sources.title: Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 (Act of June 25, 1938, ch. 676, 52 Stat. 1060)
sources.author: United States Congress
sources.publisher: United States Statutes at Large, vol. 52, p. 1060
sources.attribution: Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938, sec. 13(a).
sources.notes: Example of a minimum-wage law that left farm employees out (sec. 13(a)(6)). The words "domestic" and "household" do not occur in the 1938 text (searched), so domestic service was outside it.

sources.title: Fabric of Nations P7 provisional coefficients
sources.author: Fabric of Nations project
sources.attribution: Fabric of Nations P7 plan and completion report.
sources.notes: Values with no historical counterpart found; each row's note gives the reasoning. Provisional until P15.

provisionalRows.subject: coefficient
provisionalRows.measure: farm operators' reference wage relative to the production-worker wage
provisionalRows.note: No 1900 farm-operator income series was found (the Douglas and Lebergott series cover employees). The wage only splits an owner-operator's income between wage and profit (plan §4.1); the residual reaches farmers through profit distribution.

provisionalRows.subject: coefficient
provisionalRows.measure: shopkeepers' reference wage relative to trade employees' earnings (D 752)
provisionalRows.note: Proprietors are not in the employee series; trade employees' earnings stand in. Owner-operators earn the residual through profits.

provisionalRows.subject: coefficient
provisionalRows.measure: career enlisted pay relative to the production-worker wage
provisionalRows.note: As the P2b soldier pay (a soldier is paid as an unskilled worker); the army pay table of 1900 was not transcribed. Servicemen are not populated in P7 (plan Q2a).

provisionalRows.subject: coefficient
provisionalRows.measure: officers' pay relative to federal executive employees (D 790)
provisionalRows.note: Officers are not populated in P7 (plan Q2a; counted in Bureaucrats).

provisionalRows.subject: coefficient
provisionalRows.measure: medics' reference wage relative to clerical salaried staff (D 787)
provisionalRows.note: D 756 ($256, 1901) covers health-service employees only; physicians, half of US medics in 1900 (Webb p.443: 132,000 physicians), were self-employed and earned more. Salaried clerical pay stands in until a physician income source is transcribed.

provisionalRows.subject: coefficient
provisionalRows.measure: engineers' reference wage relative to clerical salaried staff (D 787)
provisionalRows.note: No 1900 engineers' salary series was transcribed; the salaried staff of manufacturing and railroads stand in.

provisionalRows.subject: coefficient
provisionalRows.measure: academics' reference wage relative to clerical salaried staff (D 787)
provisionalRows.note: Academics were priced at the teacher salary in P2b; teachers now have their own profession. Salaried pay stands in for professors, lawyers and writers.

provisionalRows.subject: coefficient
provisionalRows.measure: aristocrats' reference wage relative to capitalists
provisionalRows.note: Land income reaches aristocrats through profits; the wage only splits income.

provisionalRows.subject: coefficient
provisionalRows.measure: engineers' share of a heavy-industry or power building's non-manual jobs
provisionalRows.note: Plan §3.4: provisional share of the clerks' slots of heavy industry and power buildings re-mapped to engineers.
